title: Expanding AI Storage Access with NVIDIA cuObject and the NVIDIA SCADA Server SDK | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA made cuObject client/server libraries generally available, providing an RDMA wire protocol for zero-copy GPU access to object storage, and is expanding the xio-sig consortium (with Google Cloud evaluating and Microsoft planning to join the board) to cover cuObject alongside cuFile. It also launched a SCADA Server SDK for GPU-initiated fine-grained storage access, prototyped by IBM Storage Scale, under a 40+ member Storage-Next standards push.

insights.claim: AI workloads increasingly need high-speed data access not only for training but for fine-tuning, inference context, tool calls, searches and database lookups, much of it in file and object storage on-prem and in the cloud.
insights.speaker: Harish Arora
insights.so_what: Inference and agentic workloads expand the storage-performance TAM beyond training clusters.
insights.quote: AI workloads increasingly require high-speed data access for training, fine-tuning, inference context, tool calls, searches, and database lookups.

insights.claim: The need for RDMA-accelerated, zero-copy transfers that bypass server CPU memory via NICs or DPUs grows as GPU architectures get faster.
insights.speaker: Harish Arora
insights.so_what: Each GPU generation pulls through more NVIDIA networking (ConnectX/BlueField) attach, reinforcing its data-path share.
insights.quote: The need for RDMA-accelerated, zero-copy data transfers grows with faster GPU architectures.

insights.claim: An emerging class of AI data access consists of small, fine-grained I/O requests initiated by accelerators that do not fit traditional storage media or protocols.
insights.speaker: Harish Arora
insights.so_what: Implies new NAND, controller and storage-server designs optimized for GPU-initiated small I/O, a potential product cycle for flash and controller vendors.
insights.quote: an emerging class of AI data access involving small, fine-grained I/O requests initiated by accelerators that don’t fit traditional storage media or protocols
insights.locator: There is also an emerging class

insights.claim: Object storage over RDMA has lacked a common wire protocol, forcing developers into provider-specific integrations or traditional access methods.
insights.speaker: Harish Arora
insights.so_what: Whoever defines the standard wire protocol shapes the storage ecosystem; NVIDIA is positioning cuObject as that default.
insights.quote: Object storage over RDMA has also lacked a common wire protocol
insights.locator: Developers building direct access to file

insights.claim: NVIDIA announced general availability of cuObject client and server libraries, where object control runs over HTTPS/TCP while data transfers occur over RDMA, letting accelerators bypass the server CPU for higher throughput, lower latency and lower CPU use.
insights.speaker: Harish Arora
insights.so_what: Reduces CPU dependence in AI storage servers, shifting value toward GPUs, DPUs and NICs.

insights.claim: NVIDIA is expanding the xio-sig consortium to include cuObject alongside cuFile, with Google Cloud (already a cuFile maintainer) evaluating expanded participation and Microsoft looking to join the xio-sig Board.
insights.speaker: Harish Arora
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler buy-in would make NVIDIA's storage APIs a cross-cloud standard, though Google's commitment is only 'evaluating'.
insights.quote: Microsoft also looks forward to joining the xio-sig Board to improve interoperability in storage I/O.
insights.locator: Building on its involvement as a maintainer

insights.claim: xio-sig headers, the cuObject wire protocol and libxFile/xFile kernel code will only be shared once the production-ready stack passes conformance tests, and governance documents are still under review by pending board members.
insights.speaker: Harish Arora
insights.so_what: The 'open' standard is not yet open; interoperability claims remain prospective and timing-dependent.
insights.quote: The governance documents are currently under review by pending Board Members.

insights.claim: Through the Storage-Next initiative, NVIDIA leads more than 40 vendors and customers, including NAND vendors, controller vendors, storage providers, hyperscalers and application developers, to turn GPU-driven storage into open industry standards.
insights.speaker: Harish Arora
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is extending platform control down into the storage stack, with flash and controller suppliers aligning to its spec.
insights.locator: There is also an emerging class

insights.claim: The new SCADA Server SDK lets storage partners build servers that receive GPU-initiated requests from SCADA clients, fulfill them from local or remote storage and return results over RDMA, supported by a Storage Lender Service and a SCADA command-line utility.
insights.speaker: Harish Arora
insights.so_what: Creates a certification-style ecosystem for storage vendors that want to sell into GPU clusters.

insights.claim: IBM Storage demonstrated a prototype in which a SCADA client sends requests to an initial Storage Scale SCADA server built on the new SDK, a pattern NVIDIA says could support large-dataset applications like semantic search, recommender systems and fraud detection.
insights.speaker: Harish Arora
insights.so_what: IBM is an early storage vendor aligning with NVIDIA's GPU-initiated I/O path; watch for other storage vendors following.
insights.locator: IBM Storage has demonstrated a prototype
